headline: Maersk Boxship Topples Crane at Yantian
subheadline: Wind limits for berthing big boxships
insight: The 15,516 TEU Maersk Cincinnati struck a ship-to-shore crane while berthing, toppling it onto stacked boxes. No injuries reported; strong gusts reported.

sources.title: Containership Maersk Cincinnati Knocks Down Crane While Berthing at Yantian
15,516 TEU Container Ship Hits And Topples Ship-To-Shore Crane At Yantian Port In China

factCheck.notes: Facts cross-checked against at least two independent outlets or the primary statement; only verified facts used.

meta.description: On 9 November 2026 the Singapore-flagged, 366 m, 15,516 TEU container ship Maersk Cincinnati struck a ship-to-shore crane while berthing at Yantian port, Shenzhen, and the crane toppled onto containers stacked behind it. No injuries have been reported. Wind gusts of Force 8 or more were reported around the time of the approach. The Yantian District Emergency Management Bureau confirmed the incident and said an investigation is under way.
meta.question: What wind limit does your company set for berthing large boxships?
